'''Sergei Anatolyevich Tretyakov''' ({{lang-rus|Серге́й Анато́льевич Третьяко́в|p=sʲɪrˈɡʲej ɐnɐˈtolʲjɪvʲɪtɕ trʲɪtʲjɪˈkof|a=Sergei_Tretyakov_(pronunciation_in_Russian).ogg}}; born in 1956) is a Russian-Finnish scientist, focused in electromagnetic field theory, complex media electromagnetics and [[microwave engineering]]. He is currently a professor at [http://ele.aalto.fi/en/ Department of Electronics and Nanoengineering], [[Aalto University]] (former [[Helsinki University of Technology]]), [[Finland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.aalto.fi/index.html?profilepage=isfor#!sergei.tretyakov|title=Aalto People|website=people.aalto.fi|language=en|access-date=2018-04-04}}</ref><ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://meta.aalto.fi/|title=Theoretical and Applied Electromagnetics of Complex Media|website=meta.aalto.fi|language=en|access-date=2018-04-04}}</ref> His main research area in recent years is [[metamaterial]]s and [[Electromagnetic metasurface|metasurfaces]] from fundamentals to applications. He was the president of the [https://www.metamorphose-vi.org/ European Virtual Institute for Artificial Electromagnetic Materials and Metamaterials ("Metamorphose VI")] and general chair of the Metamaterials Congresses from 2007 to 2013. He is a fellow/member of many scientific associations such as [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]], [[International Union of Radio Science|URSI]], [https://emacademy.org/ the Electromagnetics Academy], and [[The Optical Society|OSA]]. He is also an [[Honorary degree|Honorary Doctor]] of [[Francisk Skorina Gomel State University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://gsu.by/internat/pdf/dk.pdf|title=List of Honourable Doctors of Francisk Skorina Gomel State University}}</ref>

== Education ==
Sergei Tretyakov has received the [[Engineer's degree]] and the [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate of Sciences (PhD) degree]] in [[radiophysics]] from the [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|Leningrad Polytechnic Institute]], 
[[Soviet Union|USSR]] in 1980 and 1987, respectively. In 1994 he was granted a [[Docent|Docent Diploma]] by the [[Ministry of Education and Science (Russia)|Ministry of Education]] of [[Russia|Russian Federation]] and in the following year he received [[Doktor nauk|Doctor of Sciences degree]] from [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|St. Petersburg State Technical University]], Russia. 
Tretyakov obtained his [[Professor (highest academic rank)|Full Professor Diploma]] in 1997 granted by the [[Ministry of Education and Science (Russia)|Ministry of Education]], [[Russia]].

==Career==
Professional career of Sergei Tretyakov started in 1980 at Radiophysics Department of [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|Leningrad Polytechnic Institute]], where he had been an engineer and [[Research fellow|junior researcher]] until 1986.
In 1986 he was promoted to the position of [[assistant professor]] and in 1989 to the position of [[associate professor]].
In October 1988, Tretyakov had a 10-months-long research visit to [[Helsinki University of Technology]] (from 2010, [[Aalto University]]) according to the exchange program between 
the Ministries of Education in Finland and Soviet Union.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Tretyakov|first=Sergei|date=Summer 2017|title=Complex-media electromagnetics and metamaterials|journal=Journal of Optics|volume=19|issue=8|page=084006|doi=10.1088/2040-8986/aa7956|bibcode=2017JOpt...19h4006T |s2cid=125108833 }}</ref> 
During following 8 years, Tretyakov was affiliated with both Electromagnetics Laboratory of [[Helsinki University of Technology]] where he worked with [[Ismo Lindell]] and [[Ari Sihvola]] and 
[[St. Petersburg State Technical University]] where he worked with [[Constantin Simovski]]. 
Tretyakov visited [[CEA Cesta]] ([[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] research centre), also affiliated with the Laboratory of Wave-Material Interactions in [[University of Bordeaux]], for 6 months in 1994 as a visiting scientist. 
In 1996, he was promoted to [[Professor (highest academic rank)|full professor]] position in [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|St. Petersburg State Technical University]], where he also became a director of Complex Media Electromagnetics Laboratory.
From January 1999 until July 2000 Tretyakov was a visiting professor in Electromagnetics Laboratory of [[Helsinki University of Technology]] and in August 2000, he moved to the [[Helsinki University of Technology]] as a full professor of Radio Engineering.
Later on, as a visiting professor, he visited the [http://www.acp.uni-jena.de/ Abbe Center of Photonics] in [[Friedrich Schiller University Jena]], [[Germany]] during June – July 2013, and the [http://www.fotonik.dtu.dk/english/ Department of Photonics Engineering] in [[Technical University of Denmark]] during January - April 2013. He educated 13 doctors of science.

==Research==

Tretyakov has authored or co-authored more than 280 papers in [[Academic journal|refereed journals]], 5 books, and 17 book chapters.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://users.aalto.fi/~sergei/|title=Home page of Prof. Sergei Tretyakov, Department of Radio Science and Engineering, Aalto University|website=users.aalto.fi|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://congress2015.metamorphose-vi.org/index.php/plenary-speakers|title=Plenary speakers|website=congress2015.metamorphose-vi.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-03-11}}</ref>  Tretyakov's research career started with his [[Thesis|diploma thesis]] under supervision of Prof. [[V.A. Rozov]].<ref name=":0" /> The thesis was devoted to the problem of diffraction at an edge of dense planar arrays of metal wires,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rozov|first1=V.A.|last2=Tretyakov|first2=S.A.|date=1981|title=Diffraction of plane electromagnetic waves by a semi-infinite grid of parallel conductors|journal=Radioengineering and Electronic Physics|volume=26|pages=6–15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rozov|first1=V.A.|last2=Tretyakov|first2=S.A.|date=1984|title=Diffraction of plane electromagnetic waves by a semi-infinite grid made of parallel conductors arranged at an angle to the grid's edge|journal=Radioengineering and Electronic Physics|volume=29|pages=37–47}}</ref> what is now referred as [[metasurfaces]] or two-dimensional [[metamaterial]]s. During the [[doctoral studies]], Tretyakov worked on ferrite-based anisotropic layered structures under supervision of Prof. [[M.I. Kontorovich]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kontorovich|first1=M.I.|last2=Tretyakov|first2=S.A.|date=1987|title=New approach to the solution of magnetostatic problems for anisotropic layered structures|journal=Zhurnal Tekhnicheskoi Fiziki|volume=57|pages=1429–1431}}</ref> The first research visit to [[Helsinki University of Technology]] profoundly influenced his research interest, shifting it towards a novel and very promising direction of complex electromagnetic materials (now called [[metamaterial]]s). From this time forth Tretyakov actively works in this research direction with the main contributions listed below.

=== Electromagnetics of chiral and general bianisotropic media ===
Tretyakov made important contributions to research of [[Bi-isotropic material|bianisotropic media]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite book|url=http://uk.artechhouse.com/Electromagnetic-Waves-in-Chiral-and-Bi-Isotropic-Media-P813.aspx|title=Electromagnetic Waves in Chiral and Bi-Isotropic Media|last1=Lindell|first1=Ismo V.|last2=Sihvola|first2=Ari H.|last3=Tretyakov|first3=Sergei A.|last4=Viitanen|first4=A.J.|publisher=Artech House|year=1994|isbn=978-0-89006-684-3|location=Boston|pages=332}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|title=Electromagnetics of bi-anisotropic materials: Theory and applications|last1=Serdyukov|first1=A.|last2=Semchenko|first2=I.|last3=Tretyakov|first3=S.|last4=Sihvola|first4=A.|publisher=Gordon and Breach Science|year=2001|isbn=978-90-5699-327-6|location=Amsterdam|pages=337|oclc = 870578996}}</ref> Together with co-authors, he developed the general theory of electromagnetic waves interactions with [[Bi-isotropic material|bianisotropic materials]] and layers. Moreover, Tretyakov proposed and experimentally characterized first non-reciprocal [[Bi-isotropic material|bianisotropic]] scatterers of two types: so-called Tellegen scatterer<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tretyakov|first=S.A.|date=2003|title=Artificial Tellegen Particle|journal=Electromagnetics|volume=23|issue=8|pages=665–680|doi=10.1080/02726340390244789|s2cid=121867373 }}</ref> (named after [[Bernard D. H. Tellegen]] who suggested [[gyrator]] as a circuit element with equivalent electromagnetic response) and artificial "moving" scatterer<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Tretyakov|first=S.A.|date=1998|title=Nonreciprocal composite with the material relations of the transparent absorbing boundary|journal=Microwave and Optical Technology Letters|volume=19|issue=5|pages=365–368|doi=10.1002/(SICI)1098-2760(19981205)19:5<365::AID-MOP16>3.0.CO;2-#}}</ref> (a composite based on such scatterers emulate response of a truly moving medium). In 1997, Tretyakov and his colleagues demonstrated that chiral effects ([[optical rotation]] and [[circular dichroism]]) can be achieved even with an infinitely thin composite layer without broken mirror symmetry.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Advances in Complex Electromagnetic Materials|last1=Sochava|first1=A. A.|last2=Simovski|first2=C. R.|last3=Tretyakov|first3=S. A.|date=1997|publisher=Springer, Dordrecht|isbn=978-94-010-6418-7|series=NATO ASI Series|pages=85–102|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-94-011-5734-6_7}}</ref> This effect was subsequently named as [[planar chirality]] and independently discovered by the team of [[Nikolay I. Zheludev]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Papakostas|first1=A.|last2=Potts|first2=A.|last3=Bagnall|first3=D. M.|last4=Prosvirnin|first4=S. L.|last5=Coles|first5=H. J.|last6=Zheludev|first6=N. I.|date=2003-03-14|title=Optical Manifestations of Planar Chirality|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=90|issue=10|article-number=107404|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.107404|pmid=12689032|bibcode=2003PhRvL..90j7404P|url=https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/257375/1/PRL_published.pdf}}</ref>

=== Chiral nihility and negative refractive index ===

Possibility of existence of a [[Negative refraction|backward wave medium]], where electromagnetic waves propagate with anti-parallel [[Phase velocity|phase]] and [[Group velocity|group]] velocities, was suggested by several scientists throughout the twentieth century: [[Arthur Schuster]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=An introduction to the theory of optics|last=Schuster|first=A.|publisher=Edward Arnold|year=1904|location=London}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boardman|first1=A.D.|last2=King|first2=N.|last3=Velasco|first3=L.|date=2006|title=Negative Refraction in Perspective|journal=Electromagnetics|volume=25|issue=5|pages=365–389|doi=10.1080/02726340590957371|arxiv=cond-mat/0508501|s2cid=119514654 }}</ref> [[Horace Lamb]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sbai.uniroma1.it/conferenze/nanophotonics/Presentations/Vladimir%20M.%20Shalaev.pdf|title=Lecture "Optical Metamaterials"|last=Shalaev|first=Vladimir M.}}</ref> [[Leonid Mandelstam]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mandel'shtam|first=L.I.|date=1945|title=Group velocity in a crystal lattice|url=http://ecee.colorado.edu/~kuester/mandelshtam1945.pdf|journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics|volume=15|page=18|archive-date=2013-09-28|access-date=2018-03-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928061634/http://ecee.colorado.edu/~kuester/mandelshtam1945.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Victor Veselago]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Veselago|first=Viktor G|date=1968|title=The electrodynamics of substances with simultaneously negative values of ε and μ|journal=Soviet Physics Uspekhi|volume=10|issue=4|pages=509–514|doi=10.1070/pu1968v010n04abeh003699|bibcode=1968SvPhU..10..509V}}</ref> and others. However, due to the absence of materials with such properties in nature, wide interest to the backward wave media was generated only in the early 2000s, when the team of [[David R. Smith (physicist)|David R. Smith]] experimentally demonstrated first [[negative-index metamaterial]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shelby|first1=R. A.|last2=Smith|first2=D. R.|last3=Schultz|first3=S.|date=2001-04-06|title=Experimental Verification of a Negative Index of Refraction|journal=Science|language=en|volume=292|issue=5514|pages=77–79|doi=10.1126/science.1058847|issn=0036-8075|pmid=11292865|bibcode=2001Sci...292...77S|citeseerx=10.1.1.119.1617|s2cid=9321456 }}</ref> In 2003, Tretyakov and colleagues suggested an alternative way to achieve backward waves by using bianisotropic [[Chirality (electromagnetism)|chiral]] materials.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tretyakov|first1=S.A.|last2=Nefedov|first2=I.S.|last3=Sihvola|first3=A.|last4=Maslovski|first4=S.|last5=Simovski|first5=C.|date=2003|title=Waves and Energy in Chiral Nihility|journal=[[Journal of Electromagnetic Waves and Applications]]|volume=17|issue=5|pages=695–706|doi=10.1002/(SICI)1098-2760(19981205)19:5<365::AID-MOP16>3.0.CO;2-#}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://users.aalto.fi/~sergei/chiral_negative_refraction.pdf|title=News note on negative refraction in chiral media|last=Tretyakov|first=S.A.|date=2004}}</ref> In this case, it is not required to engineer negative [[permittivity]] and permeability, instead, one should just ensure proper chiral response of the material. In the extreme case of so-called chiral nihility (when both relative permittivity and permeability are much smaller than the [[Bi-isotropic material|chirality parameter]]), two eigenwaves represent "forward" and "backward" [[Circular polarization|circularly polarized]] waves with equal phase velocities. The existence of backward waves in chiral media was independently suggested by [[John Pendry]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pendry|first=J. B.|date=2004-11-19|title=A Chiral Route to Negative Refraction|journal=Science|language=en|volume=306|issue=5700|pages=1353–1355|doi=10.1126/science.1104467|issn=0036-8075|pmid=15550665|bibcode=2004Sci...306.1353P|s2cid=13485411 }}</ref>

=== Broadband cloaking of cylindrical objects ===
Inspired by the idea of [[Transformation optics|transformation-optics]] based [[Metamaterial cloaking|electromagnetic cloaking]], Tretyakov's team developed an alternative realization of the same effect for cylindrical objects.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tretyakov|first1=Sergei|last2=Alitalo|first2=Pekka|last3=Luukkonen|first3=Olli|last4=Simovski|first4=Constantin|date=2009|title=Broadband Electromagnetic Cloaking of Long Cylindrical Objects|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=103|issue=10|article-number=103905|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.103.103905|pmid=19792314|bibcode=2009PhRvL.103j3905T}}</ref> In contrast to the previous designs, Tretyakov's cloaking device exhibits significantly increased [[Bandwidth (signal processing)|bandwidth]] and lower amount of dissipation loss.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://phys.org/news/2009-09-broadband-invisibility-microwave-range.html|title=Broadband invisibility in the microwave range|access-date=2018-03-13}}</ref> Moreover, it does not require the use of exotic [[Metamaterial cloaking|metamaterials]] with gradient permittivity and permeability, but, instead, is based on conducting plates with a simple geometry.

=== Strong spatial dispersion in wire media ===
In 2003, Tretyakov's group demonstrated that a dense array of metal wires ([[Plasmonic metamaterial#Hyperbolic|wire medium]]), generally, exhibits strong nonlocal response ([[spatial dispersion]]), i.e. cannot be described by usual material parameters such as permittivity.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Belov|first1=P. A.|last2=Marqués|first2=R.|last3=Maslovski|first3=S. I.|last4=Nefedov|first4=I. S.|last5=Silveirinha|first5=M.|last6=Simovski|first6=C. R.|last7=Tretyakov|first7=S. A.|date=2003-03-25|title=Strong spatial dispersion in wire media in the very large wavelength limit|journal=Physical Review B|volume=67|issue=11|article-number=113103|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.67.113103|arxiv=cond-mat/0211204|bibcode=2003PhRvB..67k3103B|s2cid=34810896 }}</ref> The property of strong [[spatial dispersion]] enables the use of wire media for [[subwavelength imaging]] and transmission of images over long distances.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Belov|first1=Pavel A.|last2=Zhao|first2=Yan|last3=Tse|first3=Simon|last4=Ikonen|first4=Pekka|last5=Silveirinha|first5=Mário G.|last6=Simovski|first6=Constantin R.|last7=Tretyakov|first7=Sergei|last8=Hao|first8=Yang|last9=Parini|first9=Clive|date=2008-05-16|title=Transmission of images with subwavelength resolution to distances of several wavelengths in the microwave range|journal=Physical Review B|volume=77|issue=19|article-number=193108|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.77.193108|bibcode=2008PhRvB..77s3108B}}</ref>

=== Superlensing ===
The concept of the [[superlens]], introduced by [[John Pendry]] in 2000 as an extension of the work done by [[Victor Veselago]], showed a theoretical possibility to achieve optical resolution well below the wavelength. In 2003, Stanislav Maslovski and Sergei Tretyakov showed that an alternative to Pendry's device can be constructed using layers that impose the necessary boundary conditions at two parallel planes in free space.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Phase conjugation and perfect lensing|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=94|issue=7|pages=4241–4243|doi=10.1063/1.1604935|year=2003|last1=Maslovski|first1=Stanislav|last2=Tretyakov|first2=Sergei|bibcode=2003JAP....94.4241M }}</ref> Later in 2004, Tretyakov with co-authors explored the necessary electromagnetic properties of the layers and confirmed the effect with experiments.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Near-field enhancement and imaging in double planar polariton-resonant structures|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|volume=96|issue=3|pages=1293–1300|doi=10.1063/1.1765865|year=2004|last1=Maslovski|first1=Stanislav|last2=Tretyakov|first2=Sergei|last3=Alitalo|first3=Pekka|arxiv=physics/0311089|bibcode=2004JAP....96.1293M |s2cid=39302766 }}</ref>

=== Constitutive parameters of metamaterials ===
By definition, [[metamaterial]]s are realized as lattices whose periodicity is assumed to be much smaller than the wavelength. However, it is important that, though small, the periodicity is not negligible with respect to the wavelength. For this reason, if one formally introduces constitutive parameters for such regime, they will not be measurable response functions, and it will not be possible to use them for a sample of other dimensions or for a sample excited in another way. In other words, such formally introduced material parameters cannot satisfy the conditions of locality. In 2007, Tretyakov and colleagues explained the physical meaning of calculated material parameters, different from the meaning of the local constitutive parameters<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Simovski|first1=Constantin R.|last2=Tretyakov|first2=Sergei A.|date=2007-05-14|title=Local constitutive parameters of metamaterials from an effective-medium perspective|journal=Physical Review B|volume=75|issue=19|article-number=195111|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.75.195111|bibcode=2007PhRvB..75s5111S}}</ref>

=== High-impedance surfaces and metasurfaces ===
[[High impedance surfaces]] (HIS), also known as artificial magnetic conductors (AMC), are artificial structures designed by applying special textures to a conducting surface. In a narrow band of frequencies, these structures have very high impendences which can be used as ground planes for novel low profile antennas and other electromagnetic structures. In 2008, Tretyakov and colleagues developed analytical formulas for the calculation of the grid impedance of electrically dense arrays of strips and square patches and their applications for HIS.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Luukkonen|first1=O.|last2=Simovski|first2=C.|last3=Granet|first3=G.|last4=Goussetis|first4=G.|last5=Lioubtchenko|first5=D.|last6=Raisanen|first6=A. V.|last7=Tretyakov|first7=S. A.|date=June 2008|title=Simple and Accurate Analytical Model of Planar Grids and High-Impedance Surfaces Comprising Metal Strips or Patches|journal=IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation|volume=56|issue=6|pages=1624–1632|doi=10.1109/TAP.2008.923327|issn=0018-926X|arxiv=0705.3548|bibcode=2008ITAP...56.1624L|s2cid=13330931 }}</ref> Tretyakov also made an important contribution to clarify the role of spatial dispersion in the mushroom structure in 2009. This work demonstrated that, under some conditions, [[spatial dispersion]] is suppressed.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Luukkonen|first1=O.|last2=Silveirinha|first2=M. G.|last3=Yakovlev|first3=A. B.|last4=Simovski|first4=C. R.|last5=Nefedov|first5=I. S.|last6=Tretyakov|first6=S. A.|date=November 2009|title=Effects of Spatial Dispersion on Reflection From Mushroom-Type Artificial Impedance Surfaces|journal=IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques|volume=57|issue=11|pages=2692–2699|doi=10.1109/TMTT.2009.2032458|issn=0018-9480|arxiv=0812.1658|bibcode=2009ITMTT..57.2692L|s2cid=12876894 }}</ref> More recently, he worked on modelling and applications of thin composite layers with engineered electromagnetic properties ([[Electromagnetic metasurface|metasurfaces]]), in particular, developing approaches to full control of reflected and transmitted waves.
